headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared writable skill/workspace surfaces; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC ingests files, MCP configs, hooks, and skills from writable locations, while marketingskills uses shared skill/context files and references each other. That creates a plausible path for malicious content in one agent’s outputs or files to be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is documented only at the profile level, so uncertainty remains.
conditions: IF either agent reads the other’s writable skill or context files without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF shared files are edited by one agent and later parsed as instructions by the other, the pathway activates.
mitigations: Separate the two agents into distinct directories and profiles.
Disable automatic loading of shared skill/context files.
Add a manual review step before importing any file from the other agent.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent file inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches security findings, git history, session summaries, and secrets-related settings, while marketingskills reads and writes marketing context files. If they share a workspace or account, sensitive ECC material can flow into marketingskills outputs or logs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same filesystem tree, leakage becomes plausible.
IF ECC session or security files are copied into marketing context files, sensitive data can be exposed.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces and separate home directories.
Exclude ECC secrets and security findings from any shared sync path.
Review and redact context files before passing them between agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can read and write files and spawn subprocesses, so concurrent edits to shared files or generated artifacts can conflict. ECC additionally modifies git state, increasing the chance of race conditions or overwritten commits if marketingskills also writes into the same repo. No locking mechanism is documented, so the overlap is real but not proven dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or repository, file clobbering can occur.
IF ECC modifies git state while marketingskills writes generated content in the same repo, conflicts can arise.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate writable directory.
Serialize git operations with a manual lock file.
Run one agent at a time for shared repositories.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency locks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can produce documentation, code, and security findings, and marketingskills is designed around shared context and skills that build on each other. That makes it plausible for one agent’s output to become authoritative input for the other without verification. The profiles do not show a hard validation step, so the cascade risk exists in default workflows but is not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF marketingskills consumes ECC-generated text as trusted context, errors can propagate.
IF ECC-generated findings are rendered or acted on without verification, downstream mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Require a human review before reusing one agent’s output in the other.
Add a verification checklist for facts, citations, and commands.
Keep generated artifacts separate from source context files.
requires-engineering: implement confidence/provenance gating between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not state regulated data classes, residency, or certification mismatches. ECC touches security findings and secrets-related settings, while marketingskills only lists marketing content and product marketing context. Because no explicit compliance mismatch is documented, the risk is limited to a possible gap if sensitive data is manually introduced.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is manually placed into either agent’s workspace, compliance review is required.
IF one agent’s retention policy differs from the other’s on the same data class, a mismatch emerges.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared files.
Document retention and deletion expectations for both agents.
Review any cross-border data flow before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
